symptom: A user task whose page has no button completing one of its outcomes — a page that only shows the task, as an agent eval generated three times — passed `check`, `check -p --references`, mx check and the build; every instance then waited at the task, with nothing anywhere reporting why
cause: No check looked at what a task page can DO: the task-signature check verifies the page's parameter (CE7410/CE7412) and stops there, and Mendix itself never requires an outcome button
file: `mdl/executor/validate_task_page_outcomes.go` (ValidateTaskPageOutcomes in validate_program.go; StoredTaskPageOutcomeViolations in cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go and exec_preflight.go)
insight: Judge reachability, not presence: an outcome counts as choosable through a `complete task` button OR a button whose microflow reaches `set task outcome` through any calls (script or stored, depth-bounded), and anything the check cannot read — a stored microflow it cannot load, a snippet, a page the script alters — makes it silent, because a warning on a page that works trains people to ignore the rule. Stored pages are read raw (GetRawUnitByName 'page'): the key names were taken from a dump of a real stored page (Forms$SetTaskOutcomeClientAction.OutcomeValue, Forms$MicroflowAction.MicroflowSettings.Microflow), not from the metamodel. Two passes, like MDL-WORKFLOW10: the script pass runs without a project; the stored pass returns only what the script pass did not, so check -p prints each once. It stays a WARNING — an outcome can be completed off the page on purpose — and it does not police the claim, which the skill's template handles (measured: an unclaimed task's complete-task button fails at runtime)
fix: MDL-WF20 warning per user/multi-user task listing the outcomes its page cannot complete, with the button to add
